reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: An oil-free coating with tethered functional segments does lose far less functional material than an oil-containing one, but the model omits wear, which removes tethered segments at roughly v*c = 2 um/yr*100 kg/m^3 = 0.2 g/m^2/yr, and the pseudo-steady oil flux (9.5 g/m^2/yr) overstates real oil release; about 80 % lower loss rate is plausible. Keeping material says little about keeping the anti-slime function, which usually fails by conditioning films and surface reconstruction, so the objective contribution is below 1 %.
key_assumption_issues: Baseline assumes 4.5 wt% free silicone oil; against an oil-free PDMS foul-release coating the comparison has no meaning
Wear loss of tethered segments is not modelled and exceeds the modelled cleavage flux
Linker cleavage rate 3e-10 1/s (half-life 73 years) is a free choice that sets the design flux
Pseudo-steady diffusion for a finite, depleting oil reservoir overstates the baseline flux
killer_risks: Anti-slime function lost by conditioning films and surface reconstruction regardless of reservoir size
Without free oil the initial slipperiness and release performance may be lower than commercial oil-containing coatings
Zwitterion-rich silicone swells and loses adhesion to the tie layer

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: Including idle periods is an improvement, but the sticking probability 0.5 and adhesion strength 15 Pa are fresh-surface lab values; after months in seawater brush surfaces lose much of their advantage, so about 25 % less retained slime is realistic, worth about 1 % of time-averaged friction with a ~5 % slime penalty.
key_assumption_issues: Sticking probability 0.5 and adhesion strength 15 Pa are free inputs from short-term lab assays and set the gain
Settlement flux used as a proxy for slime thickness; growth and consolidation not modelled
No ageing of the brush layer in the model
killer_risks: Molecular brush layer masked by conditioning films and oil and abraded within months
Bottle-brush macromers are expensive to make at the tonnage of hull coatings
Hydrolysis of siloxane anchors over years

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The 1D compliance model ignores the in-plane load spreading of the stiff skin (shear-lag length ~1.6 mm around a 5 mm base) and the viscoelastic and cupping effects of barnacles on ultra-soft beds, so about 55 % lower release stress than a commercial topcoat is realistic. Merchant ships shed most macrofouling from foul-release coatings at speed; the benefit appears after idle periods and in cleaning, so about 1.5 % of time-averaged friction; slime is unaffected.
key_assumption_issues: 1D through-thickness compliance ignores load spreading by the stiff skin, which raises the release stress
Elastic Kendall energy balance with w = 0.05 J/m^2; real barnacle cement is viscoelastic
Bed modulus 0.1 MPa is a gel whose long-term properties in seawater are uncertain
killer_risks: Punctures or cuts through the 50 um skin expose a 0.1 MPa gel bed that tears and swells, starting local failure
Ultra-soft silicone gels are usually oil-extended; extractable oil would leach
Delamination at the skin/bed interface under cyclic hull loads
